h: From the till to the tee
p: One of the handiest things about the Metrocentre is that it has its own railway station, so you can leave the car at home and hop on a train from Newcastle Central in minutes. It also has a big bus interchange, which makes it easy to get to from right across Tyneside. Ideal if you want to treat the kids to a round of golf without anyone having to worry about parking.

The centre has been a big name in North East shopping since it opened in the 1980s, and it's still the sort of place where you can spend an entire day without stepping outside. A round of adventure golf usually takes about an hour, which slots neatly between a shopping session and a meal. Book your slot first, then plan the shops around it, rather than the other way round.

A couple of family tips: give the youngest players the first shot on each hole, and keep the scoring simple so nobody ends up in tears over a triple bogey. For older groups, a small forfeit for last place adds a nice bit of drama.

If you're making more of a weekend of it, Beamish, the big open-air living museum in County Durham, is a short drive away and is brilliant for all ages. Gibside, a National Trust estate in the Derwent Valley, offers woodland walks and a grand chapel, and is perfect for a fresh-air day after all that time indoors.
